title: A 2,200-Year-Old Celtic Coin Hoard Emerges in Hungary
summary:
Archaeologists in Hungary have found more than 200 Celtic silver coins that are over 2,000 years old — one of the largest found there in decades. The coins were dug up while preparing to build an electrical substation in Hungary between 2023 and 2025, E.ON said.

The hoard dates to between the late second century B.C. and the early first century B.C., weighs 4.4 pounds, and is worth more than $2,000 as silver — but its rarity makes it priceless.

Archaeologists first found a few coins, then used metal detectors to find the rest, packed in a pot about 16 inches below ground. Eszter Kreiter of Hungary's National Archaeological Institute called it a rarity in Europe — the last find like it in Hungary was in the late 1960s.

The coins copy Greek tetradrachms, an early silver coin. They are called 'Velem,' after a Celtic hilltop settlement 10 miles west. Each coin shows a head, probably the Greek god Apollo, on one side and a rider and horse on the other. The artifacts will become part of a museum exhibition.
why_it_matters: Old coins are like clues from the past, and seeing them in a museum can help you imagine what life was like for children long ago.
